question: In uniform circular motion, which of the following physical quantities remains constant?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Uniform Circular Motion (UCM)** is defined as the motion of an object traveling along a circular path at a **constant rate of motion**. In this specific type of motion, the magnitude of the velocity, which is the **Speed**, remains **constant** throughout the duration of the movement.
 
• **Velocity** is a **vector quantity**, which means it is defined by both **magnitude and direction**. Even though the magnitude (speed) is constant in UCM, the **direction of motion** changes at every single point along the circular trajectory (tangential to the circle). *Hence, velocity is not constant.*
 
• **Acceleration** in uniform circular motion is known as **centripetal acceleration**. Its magnitude is constant (calculated as **v²/r**), but its **direction** is always pointing toward the **center of the circle**. As the object moves, this "toward the center" direction relative to the coordinate system changes. *Hence, acceleration is not constant.*
 
• **Centripetal Force** is the net force required to keep an object moving in a circle. While its magnitude (**mv²/r**) remains the same if mass, speed, and radius are constant, it is a **vector quantity** whose direction changes continuously. *Hence, centripetal force is not constant.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Speed.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kinetic Energy in UCM:**

 
 
• The **Kinetic Energy** of a particle is a **scalar quantity** given by the formula **1/2 mv²**. Since the **mass (m)** and the **speed (v)** are both constant in uniform circular motion, the **Kinetic Energy** of the object remains **constant**.
 
 
 
• **Work Done and Power:**
 
 
• In **Uniform Circular Motion**, the **centripetal force** acting on the object is always **perpendicular** to the direction of the **instantaneous displacement**.
 
• According to the physics definition of work (W = Fd cos theta), when the angle between force and displacement is **90 degrees**, the **work done** is **zero**. Consequently, the **power** delivered by the centripetal force is also **zero**.
 
 
 
• **Angular Variables:**
 
 
• The **Angular Velocity (omega)** remains constant in UCM. It represents the rate of change of the **angular displacement**.
 
• The relationship between **linear speed (v)** and **angular speed (omega)** is given by the equation **v = r * omega**, where **r** is the **radius** of the circular path.
 
 
 
• **Real-world Examples:**
 
 
• The motion of the **Moon around the Earth** is an approximation of uniform circular motion, where the **gravitational force** provides the necessary centripetal force.
 
• A **satellite** orbiting the Earth in a stable **circular orbit** maintains a constant speed while its velocity vector changes direction continuously.
 
• The tips of the **hands of a clock** or a **spinning ceiling fan** running at a constant setting are classic examples of objects performing **UCM**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Vector vs Scalar Quantities:**

 
 
• It is crucial to distinguish between **scalars** (like **speed** and **kinetic energy**) and **vectors** (like **velocity**, **acceleration**, and **force**). In UCM, only the magnitudes of the vectors are constant; the vectors themselves are not constant because their directions are in a state of flux.
 
 
 
• **Non-Uniform Circular Motion:**
 
 
• If the **speed** of the object changes while moving in a circle, it is called **Non-Uniform Circular Motion**. In such cases, there is a **tangential acceleration** in addition to the **centripetal acceleration**, and the **speed** is no longer constant.
